subject: Segmentation ledger & network narrative (SOC 2 evidence)
messages:
From: Security Team <security@veridian.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: segmentation ledger and network narrative for SOC 2

Hi David,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Veridian's audit team has asked for a concise network narrative and a segregation ledger that ties Redwood's Dedicated/Private topology back to SOC 2 control families. Specifically they want: 

- A one-page narrative describing tenant isolation model for Dedicated and VPC Private (controlplane/data plane separation, egress policy enforcement, key custody).
- A diagram with annotated dataflows (ingress, model serving, KV cache, logs) and the minimal set of zones that demonstrate boundary enforcement.
- A simple matrix showing which controls (CC6, CC7, etc.) map to the network statements.

Can you provide an initial pack and an estimate for when we can have an annotated diagram and the matrix? If you have a CAIQ/SIG mapping already, that helps shorten the review.

We also need any attachments in PDF/PNG/CSV for the evidence bundle.

Appreciate it,
Aaron Li
Security Operations | Veridian Health
security@veridian.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Security Team <security@veridian.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: segmentation ledger and network narrative for SOC 2

Aaron —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an initial high-level narrative and a compact diagram that maps the Dedicated + Private modes to our control families. The attached 'redwood_segmentation_ledger_v1.pdf' includes:

- Executive summary (one page) that explains the isolation model we use for Dedicated pools vs Private VPCs.
- Dataflow sketch showing controlplane separation, egress enforcement points, and where KMS/HSM integrations sit.
- A short appendix listing which SOC 2 / SIG entries are addressed by each network claim.

Quick notes:
- For Dedicated customers we use reserved GPU pools with tenant routing and enforced north-south egress policies at the edge gateway. The control plane (deployment, model registry, rollouts) is logically separated and runs in a customer-specific control domain where required.
- For Private (VPC-hosted) deployments, the customer maintains the network boundary; our sidecar and private control plane endpoints terminate on customer-managed subnets per our VPC peering design.

Kimberly and Marissa are looped in — Kimberly will produce an annotated diagram (PNG) and Marissa will produce the isolation matrix (CSV) that maps to SOC 2 control ids.

Can you confirm whether you prefer a SIG/CAIQ-formatted spreadsheet or the simpler mapping? We can do both, but SIG exports take an extra day.

Attached: redwood_segmentation_ledger_v1.pdf

—
David Kim
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick deliverables for Veridian SOC2 pack

Kimberly / Marissa —

Aaron wants a compact narrative + diagram + matrix by end of Friday PT. Deliverables:

1) Annotated topology (PNG, 1200px) that highlights:
  - Ingress path (customer -> edge gateway -> routing tier)
  - Serving runtime (GPU pool) with KV cache boundaries
  - Control plane endpoints (management plane) and their separation from data path
  - Egress enforcement points (edge + outbound firewall clusters)

2) Isolation matrix (CSV) with columns: component, description, evidence artifact, SOC2 control id, SIG/CAIQ mapping (if available).

3) Short change-log we can include in the bundle describing the assumptions (model of shared vs dedicated resources).

Kimberly — can you produce the annotated PNG and a small export of the diagram to include the wiring labels?
Marissa — can you draft the CSV rows for the three main surfaces (control plane, data plane, egress) using the example ledger in the attached PDF?

I will review and then send to Aaron. Let’s target end-of-day Friday. If you foresee any gaps we can't substantiate, flag them and we'll surface mitigations (eg. fallback routing or customer-specific KMS options).

Thanks,
David

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Security Team <security@veridian.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Segmentation ledger & network narrative (SOC 2 evidence)

Aaron —

Following up with the requested artifacts. Attached are:

1) redwood_segmentation_ledger_v1.pdf — one-page narrative + brief appendix (attached earlier by David).
2) segmentation_map_v2.png — annotated topology with callouts for ingress, serving pools, KV cache boundaries, and outbound enforcement clusters.
3) isolation_matrix.csv — a concise mapping from network statements to SOC 2 control ids and suggested SIG/CAIQ crosswalk notes.

Links / evidence:
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefREDWOOD-veridian-evidence
- Jira ticket where we tracked the diagram updates: INF-3421

Attachment stubs: [redwood_segmentation_ledger_v1.pdf (application/pdf), segmentation_map_v2.png (image/png), isolation_matrix.csv (text/csv)]

Notes / clarifications:
- The topology PNG is intentionally compact and annotated to reduce audit friction; it does not include internal IP ranges. If the auditor demands CIDR-level details we will need an NDA addendum and a controlled evidence handoff.
- SIG/CAIQ mapping provided in the CSV is a best-effort crosswalk. If Veridian prefers the official SIG spreadsheet format we can export that tomorrow.

Please let us know if you need the diagrams in SVG or a larger resolution for printing.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Architect | Redwood Inference
